assertions.name: embeddability_admits_four_but_generations_are_three
assertions.source: The gap that IS the generation question: the proved genus bound admits n in {3,5,7,9} while the corpus assigns three generations, leaving exactly one unexplained exclusion (n = 9).

assertions.name: continuant_ladder_monotone
assertions.source: Sanity check on the recurrence at q_0: net(T(2,n)) increases along the ladder, as a generation tower must.

assertions.name: net_ratios_do_not_reproduce_mass_ratios
assertions.source: The honest negative: the bare continuant net is not the mass map, so the ladder has no predictive content at n = 9 to test against LEP. Recorded, not repaired with a fitted scale.

description: EXPLORATORY probe of the three-generation question (bean qou-4dxs), which the corpus records as 'nowhere addressed'. Locates it precisely: `torus-embeddable-complete-proof` PROVES the genus bound admits n in {3,5,7,9} for T(2,n), while `lepton-continuant-recurrence` assigns only n = 3,5,7 to e/mu/tau. The generation count IS the exclusion of T(2,9). Reports that the primality condition which would close it appears exactly once in the corpus, as an underived parenthetical, and tests the ladder's own predictive content using the corpus's Morgan-Voyce recurrence. No derivation is claimed and nothing is wired.

problem_localisation.embeddability_bound: g(T(m,n)) = (m-1)(n-1)/2 <= g(Sigma_4) = 4; for m = 2, n <= 9, so the odd coprime values are n in {3,5,7,9} -- FOUR admissible knots (PROVED, torus-embeddable-complete-proof)
problem_localisation.generation_assignment: T(2,n) for n = 3,5,7 -> e, mu, tau -- THREE generations (lepton-continuant-recurrence)
problem_localisation.the_gap: the generation count is exactly the exclusion of T(2,9); 'why three generations' reduces to the single question 'what excludes n = 9?'
problem_localisation.why_this_is_progress: it converts a problem the corpus records as 'nowhere addressed, prior to all mixing parameters' into one well-posed lemma about one knot

primality_condition_is_asserted_not_deri.consequence: n odd prime AND n <= 9 gives n in {3,5,7}, hence exactly three generations, in two lines -- but ONLY if primality is derived. It is not. This is stated as the gap it is; no two-line derivation of the generation count is claimed.
primality_condition_is_asserted_not_deri.candidate_structural_reason: For odd n >= 3, n factors into smaller odd windings iff n is composite, so 'n odd prime' and 'n is not a harmonic of a smaller odd winding' are the SAME condition. sigma^9 = (sigma^3)^3 is a harmonic of the first generation; 3, 5, 7 admit no such factorization. This is a hypothesis to be proved or refuted, not an argument -- the braid word of every n factors trivially, so the content is entirely in why factorization through a smaller ODD winding should forbid a generation assignment.

validation_FAILED_net_is_not_the_mass_ma.verdict: The bare continuant net does NOT reproduce the lepton mass ratios: net(7)/net(5) = 1.2408 against an observed tau/mu of 16.817. The net ratios are O(1) while the mass ratios are O(10^2), so net(T(2,n)) is a normal-form coefficient, not a mass. This is recorded as a failed validation rather than repaired by introducing a scale factor -- fitting one here would be exactly the laundering the anti-fit discipline forbids.
validation_FAILED_net_is_not_the_mass_ma.consequence_for_this_probe: Because the mass map is not established, this probe CANNOT compute what T(2,9) would weigh, and therefore cannot check it against the LEP exclusion. The intended decisive test is BLOCKED, and that blockage is the finding: the corpus assigns T(2,n) to generations without a wired map from the continuant to a mass, so the ladder currently has no predictive content at n = 9 to falsify.

what_would_close_it.route_A_derive_primality: Prove that a composite odd winding cannot carry a generation -- e.g. that the T(2,ab) Hecke normal form or Markov trace factors through T(2,a) in a way that forbids an independent fibre assignment. This would derive the generation count from the genus bound, and is the route with an actual payoff (3 generations, not merely <= 4).
what_would_close_it.route_B_wire_the_mass_map: Establish the map from net(T(2,n)) to a lepton mass. Then T(2,9) makes a numerical prediction and the LEP bound (no 4th charged lepton below ~45 GeV, N_nu = 2.984 +/- 0.008) either refutes the ladder or forces the truncation. Prerequisite for any falsification.
what_would_close_it.route_C_check_the_meson_tower: The same T(2,n) ladder indexes the meson tower (lepton-meson-torus-knot-dictionary). If the meson side DOES populate n = 9, then n = 9 is admissible in general and the exclusion is specific to the lepton fibre -- which would refute the harmonic hypothesis as stated and relocate the question.
what_would_close_it.priority: C is cheapest and can REFUTE the harmonic hypothesis outright; A is the one that pays; B is prerequisite to any numerical falsification.
